verdict.rationale: Claude Code is itself an agentic AI assistant: users describe tasks in plain language, and it plans, edits files across the codebase, runs commands, handles git workflows and PRs, and accepts tasks from Slack, the web or GitHub, with documented multi-agent delegation. Community reports confirm real daily use, though some users report unreliable results (e.g., failed self-verification). missing for 10: consistent independent corroboration that delegated tasks complete reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Describe what you want in plain language. Claude Code plans the approach, writes the code across multiple files, and verifies it works.

Claude Code handles the tedious tasks that eat up your day: writing tests for untested code, fixing lint errors across a project, resolving merge conflicts, updating dependencies, and writing release notes.
A lead agent coordinates the work, assigns subtasks, and merges results.
Route tasks from team chat: mention @Claude in Slack with a bug report and get a pull request back
helps you code faster by executing routine tasks, explaining complex code, and handling git workflows -- all through natural language commands
